translationRepairs: Even under ideal sage rule, severe sanctions remained necessary against major disorder before universal compliance was achieved.
In the age of Yao and Shun, even at the height of good government, they still exiled Gonggong, banished Huandou, deported the Sanmiao, and executed Gun; only then did all under heaven submit.
唐虞之際 names the Yao-Shun age, and 流共工，放讙兜，竄三苗，殛鯀 lists four concrete punishments omitted by the current idiomatic paraphrase; the proposed restoration matches that wording and 然後天下服.
Different states specialized in different military institutions to seek advantage.
King Min of Qi drew strength from skilled fighters, King Hui of Wei rose through elite troops, and King Zhao of Qin prevailed through crack soldiers.
齊愍、魏惠、秦昭 name three rulers, and 技擊、武卒、銳士 name their distinct forces; the current idiomatic line erases all of that, while the proposal restores the attributions accurately.
By balancing bureaucrats, strategists, diplomats, and ritual specialists, Gaozu aligned civil and military governance into a coherent founding program.

Gaozu employed Xiao He and Cao Shen in civil administration, used Zhang Liang and Chen Ping for strategy, gave free rein to Lu Jia and Li Yiji in persuasion, and established Shusun Tong’s ceremonial system; civil and military complemented each other, and the broad program was realized.

蕭、曹、良、平、陸、酈、叔孫通 are seven named advisers with civil, strategic, persuasive, and ritual roles; replacing them with generic occupational groups is a real omission, and the expanded names are the standard referents.
By the middle sixth year he again issued an edict: "Those who increase flogging—some die before the beating is finished; I deeply pity this.
By the middle sixth year, he again issued an edict: "Those subjected to additional flogging sometimes die before the strokes are completed; I deeply pity them."
加笞者 are persons subjected to added flogging who may die before the strokes finish (或至死而笞未畢); the original literal wrongly makes them agents who 'increase flogging.'
The offices of Zhou employed the procedures of the Five Hearings, Eight Deliberations, Three Inquiries, Three Pardons, and Three Amnesties.
The offices of Zhou employed the procedures of the Five Hearings, Eight Deliberations, Three Inquiries, Three Pardons, and Three Exemptions.

In the Zhou offices list, 三赦 is the Three Exemptions (distinct from general amnesty), already rendered that way in the chapter's literal for this unit; 'Amnesties' mislabels the category beside 三刺 and 三宥.
He emphasized mercy for frail elders swept into penal machinery despite low social threat.

'I think of old people whose hair and teeth have fallen, blood and qi declined, with no violent rebellious heart; now some are trapped in legal text, seized in prisons, unable to finish their lifespan—I deeply pity this.'
Preceded by 又下詔曰, the unit is Emperor Xuan's first-person edict (朕念夫耆老之人…朕甚憐之); the current idiomatic third-person gloss drops the quoted speech.
Local doubtful cases were escalated to higher prefectural review.
From now on, when county and district officials have doubtful prison cases, each should refer them to the relevant 2,000-shi official, and that official shall report the fitting charge.

自今以來 starts a directive that county and district doubtful cases (縣道官獄疑者) be referred to the affiliated 2,000-shi official, who reports the fitting charge; the current idiomatic summary invents 'prefectural review' and drops that procedure.
Unresolved matters moved upward to central judicial review.
What they cannot decide all transfer to the Commandant of Justice, who should also report.
皆移廷尉 names the Commandant of Justice and requires that office also report (廷尉亦當報之); the current idiomatic paraphrase omits both the office and the reporting duty.
Mass incarceration and high execution counts are cited as causes of unresolved social disharmony.

Now those executed by punishment in the commanderies and kingdoms number in the tens of thousands each year; there are over two thousand prisons under heaven; how many die unjustly, overlapping beyond count! If prisoners do not decrease by even one, this is why harmonious qi has not fully spread.

The Chinese gives yearly executions in the tens of thousands, over two thousand prisons, overlapping unjust deaths, and the causal claim that if prisons do not decrease by even one, harmonious qi remains incomplete; the current idiomatic line is only a gloss.
The text attributes penal overgrowth to moral-institutional failure, socioeconomic stress, elite predation, and uneven enforcement.

Looking to why prison penalties proliferate like this: ritual teaching is not established, penal law is not clear, the people are often poor, powerful men pursue private ends, crimes are not promptly caught, and prison officers adjudicate unevenly—these cause it.
原獄刑所以蕃若此者 introduces six concrete causes ending in 之所致也; the current idiomatic meta-summary ('the text attributes…') invents editorial framing and drops those stated causes.
